English: Timber Dock
A rough wooden quay and makeshift storage for small boats, providing minimal naval support and a base for simple boat maintenance.
Fishing Wharf
A bustling wharf with basic warehouses and fishing piers, supporting both local fleets and economic development.
Boat Slip
Basic slipways and crude sheds for sheltering and repairing small boats, improving readiness and local economy.
Covered Slipway
Large timber-and-tile slipways with covered workspaces allow year-round shipbuilding and rapid deployment of new vessels.
Boatworks
A small yard with covered workspaces for constructing and refitting military launches, expanding naval preparedness.
Small Shipyard
A modest stone-and-timber yard for building and maintaining patrol craft, with guarded stores and organized labor.
Expanded Dockyard
Multiple piers, fortified stores, and expanded workshops enable the outfitting of larger ships and support for marines.
Naval Yard
A fortified naval yard with stone quays, tall cranes, armories, and barracks, supporting the construction and maintenance of war galleys.
Harbor Shipyard
A major harbor complex with fortified seawalls, deepwater berths, and advanced workshops for outfitting large fleets and merchant vessels.
Grand Shipyard
A vast, bustling shipyard complex with monumental slipways, dry docks, fortified walls, and command towers, capable of supporting a powerful war fleet and controlling the sea lanes.
